review_evidence: Every acl2-customization-files/*.lisp file is one or two lines invoking an existing setting command such as set-waterfall-parallelism, set-compile-fns, set-gag-mode, or serialization/bookdata settings.
The customization files introduce no defun, defmacro, defthm, defconst, or other reusable declaration; they only select runtime/certification behavior.

doc/home-page.lisp defines topic-to-url-list, constants, write-home-page, and a macro; doc/write-acl2-code-size.lisp defines a reporting function/macro, so those files are retained under the lossless interface rule.

rules.content_invariant: All selected files contain only comments plus calls to existing ACL2 configuration setters; none defines a function, macro, theorem, constant, datatype, interface, or proof artifact.
evidence: bookdata.lisp is only (f-put-global 'write-bookdata t state), while the parallel-* and serial files only call set-waterfall-parallelism.
no-serialize.lisp, set-compile-fns.lisp, and set-gag-mode-nil.lisp similarly contain only configuration calls and optional comments.
rules.rationale: Remove ACL2 runtime/certification customization snippets that only invoke pre-existing settings.

summary: Reviewed the ACL2 miscellaneous-subtree unit. The acl2-customization-files subtree is pure invocation-level runtime/certification configuration and is excluded; the two doc/*.lisp files define executable ACL2 functions/macros and are retained because excluding them would hide unique declarations.
